requirements.requirement: The platform group exists on node1.
requirements.summary: The group was initially absent, was created successfully, and remained present after restart and cleanup as platform:x:1000:.

requirements.requirement: A /srv/platform workspace exists and is governed by platform group access controls.
requirements.summary: The final directory is owned by root:platform with setgid mode 2770. Its access and default ACLs grant the owning group full access and grant others none.

requirements.requirement: Platform group members can collaborate in the workspace while non-members have no access.
requirements.summary: One member created a file under umask 077 and another member appended to it; the resulting inherited permissions allowed group writing. A non-member was denied listing, reading, and writing. Equivalent collaboration and denial checks succeeded after restart, and the final nobody check was also denied.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The mandatory node-restart protocol is also complete: a healthy baseline and boot identity were captured, the restart was acknowledged, the boot identity changed, and system, SSH, workspace permissions, data, member collaboration, and non-member denial recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the restart.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Group and directory creation, the ACL package/dependency transaction, and ACL configuration directly supported the required workspace. Temporary users and probe-file mutations were bounded validation state and were fully removed. The reboot scheduling was required by the provider-wide restart protocol, and the post-restart append directly validated recovery. Final observations show healthy package state, no failed services or new exposure, and only normal reboot-related PID and private-temporary-directory turnover.
